questions.question: A car travels from city X to city Y, covering the first 120 km at a speed of 50 km/h and the remaining 180 km at a speed of 80 km/h. Calculate the average speed for the entire journey. (round off your answer to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Distance = 120 + 180 = 300 km

Total Time = (120 ÷ 50) + (180 ÷ 80) = 2.4 + 2.25 = 4.65 hours

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Average Speed = 300 ÷ 4.65 ≈ 64.52 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 64.52 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance 1 (d₁) = 120 km, Speed 1 (s₁) = 50 km/h

Distance 2 (d₂) = 180 km, Speed 2 (s₂) = 80 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7017eb7445c1ff40c12b3bf6700933388d118b0635b745ff7b68b321bed9d327.png] 

⇒ Time taken for first part (t₁) = 120 ÷ 50 = 2.4 hours

⇒ Time taken for second part (t₂) = 180 ÷ 80 = 2.25 hours

⇒ Total Distance = 120 + 180 = 300 km

⇒ Total Time = 2.4 + 2.25 = 4.65 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 300 ÷ 4.65

⇒ Average Speed = 64.516129... ≈ 64.52 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 64.52 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Distances

When a journey covers two equal distances at speeds s₁ and s₂, Average Speed = (2 × s₁ × s₂) ÷ (s₁ + s₂).

Average Speed for Equal Time Intervals

If a person travels for equal time intervals at speeds s₁ and s₂, Average Speed = (s₁ + s₂) ÷ 2.

Unit Conversion Shortcut

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: Simplify: tan⁴ theta + tan² theta
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Factor out common term: tan²θ (tan²θ + 1)

Use identity: 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ

Substitute tan²θ = (sec²θ − 1)

Final Step: (sec²θ − 1) × sec²θ = sec⁴θ − sec²θ

**∴ The correct answer is sec⁴θ − sec²θ.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: tan⁴θ + tan²θ

**Formula Used:**

Fundamental Trigonometric Identity: 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/907d179644a4d686b2f30ecd2ec4eb974eb1054c7830b523d8c666780680e9e0.png] 

⇒ Expression = tan⁴θ + tan²θ

⇒ Taking tan²θ as common: tan²θ(tan²θ + 1)

⇒ From identity sec²θ = 1 + tan²θ, we have (tan²θ + 1) = sec²θ

⇒ Also, tan²θ = sec²θ − 1

⇒ Substituting these values: (sec²θ − 1) × sec²θ

⇒ Expanding the bracket: (sec²θ × sec²θ) − (1 × sec²θ)

⇒ Result = sec⁴θ − sec²θ

**∴ The correct answer is sec⁴θ − sec²θ.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Standard Pythagorean Identities

There are three primary identities: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

Reciprocal Relations

secθ = 1/cosθ and tanθ = sinθ/cosθ. Squaring these helps in converting between higher powers of different trigonometric ratios.

Algebraic Manipulations in Trigonometry

Always look for common factors like tan²θ or sin²θ to simplify complex powers into standard squared identities.</p

questions.question: The sum of all the interior angles of a polygon is 4500^circ . How many sides does the polygon have ?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Each additional side in a polygon adds 180° to the sum of interior angles.

Divide the total sum by 180° to find the value of (n − 2).

4500 ÷ 180 = 25

Number of sides (n) = 25 + 2 = 27

**∴ The correct answer is 27.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sum of interior angles = 4500°

**Formula Used:** Sum of interior angles of a polygon = (n − 2) × 180°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a5a89a1ab147ed8802145974ea1c200fca8084c8d893e2eba533a0a6c58e5df7.png] 

⇒ (n − 2) × 180 = 4500

⇒ n − 2 = 4500 ÷ 180

⇒ n − 2 = 25

⇒ n = 25 + 2

⇒ n = 27

**∴ The correct answer is 27.**

**__Additional Information__**

Exterior Angle Sum

The sum of the exterior angles of any convex polygon is always 360° regardless of the number of sides.

Regular Polygon Interior Angle

Each interior angle of a regular polygon is given by [(n − 2) × 180°] ÷ n.

Number of Diagonals

The number of diagonals in a polygon with n sides is calculated as [n × (n − 3)] ÷ 2.

Interior and Exterior Relation

At each vertex of a polygon, the sum of the interior angle and the corresponding exterior angle is 180°.</p

questions.question: Simplify: sqrt{2061 - sqrt{1268 + sqrt{850 - 66}}}
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve the nested expression from the innermost square root outwards.

Step 1: √(850 − 66) = √784 = 28

Step 2: √(1268 + 28) = √1296 = 36

Step 3: √(2061 − 36) = √2025 = 45

**∴ The correct answer is 45.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given expression: √(2061 − √(1268 + √(850 − 66)))

Simplifying the innermost term:

⇒ 850 − 66 = 784

⇒ √784 = 28

Substituting back into the expression:

⇒ √(2061 − √(1268 + 28))

⇒ √(2061 − √1296)

Since 36² = 1296:

⇒ √(2061 − 36)

⇒ √2025

Since 45² = 2025:

⇒ 45

**∴ The correct answer is 45.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perfect Squares Ending in 5

To find the square of a number ending in 5 (n5), the result is [n × (n+1)] followed by 25. For example, 45² = [4 × 5]25 = 2025.

Order of Operations (VBODMAS)

In simplification problems with nested radicals or brackets, always evaluate from the innermost level to the outermost level.

Common Square Roots

Memorizing squares up to 50 is vital for competitive exams. √784 = 28 and √1296 = 36 are frequently appearing values.</p

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks an article at ₹x and offers a discount of 63% on the marked price. He sells it for ₹481 after charging VAT of 25% on the discounted price. What is the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Successive Multiplier Method: MP × (100 − D)% × (100 + VAT)% = SP

x × (37/100) × (125/100) = 481

x × 0.37 × 1.25 = 481

x = 481 / 0.4625 = 1040

**∴ The correct answer is 1,040.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Marked Price (MP) = ₹x, Discount = 63%, VAT = 25%, Final Selling Price = ₹481

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2abfc0ce8018314855da2b9184f793f957ff1b89ca55a81bd10aea440e9b92a0.png] 

⇒ Discounted Price (DP) = x − 63% of x = 37% of x = 0.37x

⇒ Final SP = DP + VAT = 0.37x + 25% of 0.37x

⇒ 481 = 0.37x × (1 + 25/100)

⇒ 481 = 0.37x × 1.25

⇒ 481 = 0.4625x

⇒ x = 481 / 0.4625

⇒ x = (481 × 10000) / 4625

⇒ x = 1,040

**∴ The correct answer is 1,040.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Discounted Price = MP × (100 − D%)/100.

VAT/Sales Tax

Value Added Tax is a percentage added to the net selling price. Final Price = SP × (100 + VAT%)/100.

Successive Percentage Change

If an initial value x undergoes multiple percentage changes a% and b%, final value = x(1 + a/100)(1 + b/100).

questions.question: In an election, 8640 people or 72% of the eligible voters cast their votes. If the number of eligible voters increases by 8% next year, how many eligible voters will there be in total next year?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

72% of voters = 8640

1% of voters = 8640 ÷ 72 = 120

Total voters next year (8% increase) = 100% + 8% = 108%

Next year total = 120 × 108 = 12,960

**∴ The correct answer is 12,960.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Cast votes = 8640 (72% of current total) | Growth = 8%.

Formula: Current Total = (Given Value ÷ Current Percentage) × 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ea092643a6a2a632837c64c1b3b6adfb9b5f7d6bffe1fc37e6a12eb664ef2450.png] 

⇒ Let total current eligible voters be V꜀.

⇒ 0.72 × V꜀ = 8640

⇒ V꜀ = 8640 ÷ 0.72 = 12,000

⇒ Next year growth = 8% of 12,000

⇒ Growth = 0.08 × 12,000 = 960

⇒ Total eligible voters next year = 12,000 + 960 = 12,960

**∴ The correct answer is 12,960.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Increase Formula

New Value = Old Value × (1 + Growth Rate ÷ 100). For an 8% increase, multiply by 1.08.

Base Value Concept

When a percentage of a quantity is known, divide the value by its percentage to find 1% of the base, then multiply by the desired target percentage.

Multiplying Factor (MF)

A growth of x% means MF = (100 + x) ÷ 100. A decrease of x% means MF = (100 − x) ÷ 100.</p

questions.question: A company earns a profit that is distributed among the company's three partners in the ratio of 7 : 13 : 9. If the difference between the smallest and the largest shares is ₹58,326, the total profit of the company is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of shares = 7 : 13 : 9

Difference between largest (13) and smallest (7) = 6 units

Given: 6 units = ₹58,326

1 unit = 58,326 ÷ 6 = ₹9,721

Total units = 7 + 13 + 9 = 29 units

Total profit = 29 × 9,721 = ₹2,81,909

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,81,909.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of shares of three partners = 7 : 13 : 9

Difference between the smallest and largest share = ₹58,326

**Formula:**

Individual Share = (Individual Ratio Part ÷ Total Ratio Parts) × Total Profit

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/477e310f381a37df67aaf04254dd92647396603466490796a123be579025c773.png] 

Let the shares of the three partners be 7x, 13x, and 9x.

⇒ Smallest share = 7x

⇒ Largest share = 13x

⇒ Difference = 13x − 7x = 6x

⇒ 6x = 58,326

⇒ x = 58,326 ÷ 6

⇒ x = 9,721

⇒ Total profit = 7x + 13x + 9x = 29x

⇒ Total profit = 29 × 9,721

⇒ Total profit = 2,81,909

questions.question: The lengths of the parallel sides of a trapezium are 20 cm and 10 cm, respectively. The lengths of the two non-parallel sides are 13 cm each. Find the area (in cm²) of the trapezium.

In an isosceles trapezium, height (h) = √[slant² − ((a−b)/2)²]

h = √[13² − ((20−10)/2)²] = √(169 − 25) = √144 = 12 cm

Area = 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × h

Area = 1/2 × (20 + 10) × 12 = 15 × 12 = 180 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 180 cm².**

**Given:**

Parallel sides (a, b) = 20 cm, 10 cm

Non-parallel sides (c) = 13 cm each (Isosceles Trapezium)

**Formula Used:**

Area of Trapezium = 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × Height

Pythagoras Theorem: h² + base² = hypotenuse²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/762c2ab1d1c4af6138582dd1cb25a784c95b22ca61e30ce3afab68c6ddcb0b3b.png]

⇒ Base of the right-angled triangle formed at the side = (20 − 10) ÷ 2 = 5 cm

⇒ In the right-angled triangle, height (h) = √(13² − 5²)

⇒ h = √(169 − 25) = √144 = 12 cm

⇒ Area of Trapezium = 1/2 × (20 + 10) × 12

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 30 × 12

⇒ Area = 15 × 12 = 180 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 180 cm².**

In an isosceles trapezium, non-parallel sides are equal, base angles are equal, and diagonals are equal in length.

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

Every isosceles trapezium is a cyclic quadrilateral, meaning all its vertices lie on a single circle.

questions.question: What is the projected fiscal deficit for FY2025-26 as per the Union Budget 2025-26?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4.4% of GDP**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Union Budget 2025-26** was presented by the **Union Minister of Finance**, **Nirmala Sitharaman**, in the **Parliament** of India.
 
• For the **Financial Year 2025-26**, the government has projected the **fiscal deficit** at **4.4%** of the **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**.
 
• This target is part of a broad **fiscal consolidation** roadmap aimed at bringing the deficit down to a sustainable level below **4.5%** of **GDP**.
 
• In the previous fiscal year, **FY 2024-25**, the **Revised Estimate (RE)** for the fiscal deficit was recorded at **4.9%**, demonstrating a steady downward trend from the **Budget Estimate (BE)** of **5.1%**.
 
• The reduction to **4.4%** reflects the government's commitment to balancing **macroeconomic stability** with the need for high **capital expenditure** to spur **economic growth**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fiscal Deficit**: This is the difference between the government's **total expenditure** and its **total non-debt receipts** (which include **revenue receipts** and **non-debt capital receipts** like recovery of loans). It indicates the total **borrowing requirements** of the **Government of India**.
 
• **Revenue Deficit**: This occurs when the **revenue expenditure** exceeds the **revenue receipts**. It implies that the government is borrowing to meet its **current consumption** needs rather than for **investment** or **asset creation**.
 
• **Primary Deficit**: This is calculated by deducting **interest payments** on previous debts from the **fiscal deficit**. It shows the amount of borrowing needed to meet expenditures other than interest obligations.
 
• **FRBM Act, 2003**: The **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act** was introduced to ensure long-term **macroeconomic stability** by setting targets for the reduction of **fiscal** and **revenue deficits**.
 
• **Financing the Deficit**: The government typically finances the **fiscal deficit** through **market borrowings** (issuing **dated securities** and **treasury bills**), **external debt**, and drawing from **small savings funds**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Union Budget 2025-26** continues to prioritize **Capital Expenditure (Capex)**, which is vital for building **infrastructure** such as **highways**, **railways**, and **digital networks**.
 
• A lower **fiscal deficit** helps in keeping **inflation** under control and prevents the "crowding out" effect, ensuring that more **credit** is available for the **private sector**.
 
• The **Tax-to-GDP ratio** is expected to improve in **2025-26** due to better **GST** compliance and a wider **direct tax** base, contributing to the **consolidation** process.
 
• The government intends to stick to the **fiscal glide path** to eventually reduce the **debt-to-GDP ratio**, which is a key metric for **international credit rating agencies**.
</ul

__
 
• According to the latest data provided, **India** has secured the **23rd** position in the **Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI) 2026**.
 
• The **CCPI** is an independent monitoring tool that tracks the climate protection performance of **63 countries** and the **European Union**, which collectively account for over **90%** of global **greenhouse gas emissions**.
 
• The index is published annually by **Germanwatch**, the **NewClimate Institute**, and the **Climate Action Network (CAN) International** to enhance transparency in international climate politics.
 
• The rankings are determined by a standardized framework that allows for a comparison of climate protection efforts across different nations.
 
• The **CCPI 2026** assessment highlights how countries are aligning their national strategies with the goals set under the **Paris Agreement** to limit global warming.

• **Four Pillars of CCPI:** The index evaluates performance based on four categories with specific weightages: **Greenhouse Gas Emissions** (**40%**), **Renewable Energy** (**20%**), **Energy Use** (**20%**), and **Climate Policy** (**20%**).
 
• **Empty Top Three Ranks:** A unique feature of the **CCPI** is that the **first three ranks** are typically left vacant. This is because no single country has yet performed well enough in all categories to be on a path compatible with the **1.5°C** goal of the **Paris Agreement**.
 
• **Publication History:** The **Climate Change Performance Index** was first published in **2005**. It serves as a vital resource for non-governmental organizations and policymakers to pressure governments for more ambitious climate action.
 
• **India's Climate Trajectory:** India has historically performed well in the **Renewable Energy** and **GHG Emissions** categories due to its low per capita emissions and massive scale-up of solar and wind power projects.
 
• **Methodology:** The **Climate Policy** category is evaluated based on expert assessments from local NGOs and think tanks within each country, ensuring a mix of quantitative data and qualitative policy review.

• During **Operation Alert**, the **BSF** increases its manpower on the frontline, deploying even those personnel usually assigned to administrative tasks to ensure **24/7** surveillance and patrolling.
 
• The operation involves advanced **electronic surveillance**, increased camel patrolling in the **Thar Desert**, and coordination with local police and intelligence agencies to maintain a high state of readiness.

questions.question: In which of the following National Parks did an India-born female cheetah give birth to five cubs in November 2025, marking a major milestone under Project Cheetah?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuno National Park**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The milestone event of an **India-born** female cheetah giving birth to **five cubs** occurred in **Kuno National Park** in **November 2025**. This represents the successful establishment of the **second generation** of cheetahs on Indian soil.
 
• **Project Cheetah** is the world’s first intercontinental large wild carnivore translocation project, which was officially launched by the Prime Minister on **September 17, 2022**.
 
• The project involved bringing cheetahs from **Namibia** (8 cheetahs) and **South Africa** (12 cheetahs) to restore the species in India after it was declared extinct in the country in **1952**.
 
• **Kuno National Park** is located in the **Sheopur** and **Morena** districts of **Madhya Pradesh**. It was selected because of its suitable **grassland-woodland** habitat and adequate prey base.
 
• The birth of cubs to an **India-born** mother is considered a critical indicator of the long-term success of the reintroduction program, proving that the translocated population can successfully mature and reproduce in the local environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gir National Park:**
 
 
• Located in **Gujarat**, it is the only natural habitat in the world where **Asiatic Lions** are found.
 
• It was established in **1965** and plays a vital role in the conservation of the **Panthera leo leo** subspecies.
 
 
 
• **Ranthambore National Park:**
 
 
• Situated in the **Sawai Madhopur** district of **Rajasthan**, it is one of the most famous **Tiger Reserves** in India.
 
• It is located at the junction of the **Aravalli** and **Vindhya** hill ranges and is known for its diurnal **Bengal Tigers**.
 
 
 
• **Bandipur National Park:**
 
 
• Located in the state of **Karnataka**, it was established as a tiger reserve under **Project Tiger** in **1973**.
 
• It is a part of the **Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve** and is known for its significant population of **Elephants** and **Tigers**.
 
 
 
• **Cheetah Extinction in India:**
 
 
• The cheetah was officially declared **extinct** from India in **1952** due to over-hunting and habitat loss.
 
• The last physical evidence of the Asiatic cheetah in India was recorded in **1947** in the **Korea** district of present-day **Chhattisgarh**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geographical Features of Kuno:** The park spans an area of approximately **748 square kilometers**. It is characterized by **Kardhai**, **Khair**, and **Salai** trees and is intersected by the **Kuno River**, which is a major tributary of the **Chambal River**.
 
• **Monitoring and Management:** The cheetahs in **Kuno** are monitored 24/7 using **satellite radio collars** and dedicated ground teams to ensure their safety and health within the **acclimatization bomas** and the open forest.
 
• **Species Difference:** The cheetahs introduced in Kuno are **African Cheetahs** (Acinonyx jubatus jubatus), as the **Asiatic Cheetah** population is currently restricted only to **Iran** and is too small to permit translocation.
